data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 limits its causal mechanism to preventing 'single-point-of-failure orchestration bugs' and 'Black Swan systemic risks,' but the problem asks about correlated failure broadly, not merely orchestration-plane failures. A decentralized network can still suffer correlated failure from shared protocol-level vulnerabilities, shared upstream dependencies, or common-mode environmental triggers—failures that are correlated but have nothing to do with a unified control plane. By restricting its causal argument to the absence of a unified control plane, SRC_003 does not establish that decentralization is more resilient to correlated failure in general; it only addresses one specific failure class, leaving the broader claim under-mechanized relative to the problem's scope.
